text:
incident-bot: Pager: datadog.ingest.delay triggered for service=telemetry (alert A-12345) — metric ingest lag > 120s for 12m. Escalating to @Alex (oncall) :rotating_light:

Alex (oncall): got the page, pulling up dd dashboards now. metrics timeline looks very sparse around 02:14 UTC. https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/12345 -> lots of gaps

Jordan (SRE): seeing 502s from Datadog ingestion API in forwarder logs: 'upstream reset by peer'. This started ~02:02. Traces and events also delayed.

Maya (eng-ops): confirmed — traces+metrics both showing ingestion lag in us-east. Customer telemetry missing for last ~15m in the console.

Ella (product): customers pinging support. Is this only the hosted telemetry pipeline? Does Dedicated telemetry still work?

Alex (oncall): Dedicated uses internal prometheus scraping and is OK. Hosted pipelines push to Datadog; we're seeing blindspots in hosted dashboards. Quick mitigation plan: 1) throttle non-critical metric pushes 2) enable CW fallback for alerts 3) open/track ticket with Datadog 4) notify support & product.

Jordan (SRE): throttling now — running:```bash
kubectl -n telemetry exec deploy/metric-forwarder -- /bin/sh -c "export DD_BATCH=0.5; export DD_FLUSH_INTERVAL=60; pkill -HUP metric-forwarder"
```
-> applied, forwarder now batching less frequently.

Alex (oncall): confirmed config change, metrics push rate down. Backlog still increasing but ingest API 502s reduced.

datadog-bot: Datadog status: "Partial ingestion delays in US-EAST affecting a subset of customers. Engineers investigating." https://status.datadoghq.com/incidents/abc123 (update 02:22 UTC)

Maya (eng-ops): flipping alert routing to CloudWatch fallback for infra.alerts and cpu/mem thresholds. Editing routing rule now (telemetry-routing -> cw-proxy).

Alex (oncall): documenting blindspot in incident runbook (runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/telemetry-runbook). Noting customer impact: dashboards stale for ~15m; no functional impact to inference requests. Recommend short status page message.

Ella (product): drafting status: "We are seeing delayed telemetry ingestion from a third-party observability provider. No impact to inference or customer data — only dashboards and recent metrics. Our SREs are actively mitigating and monitoring." Will post shortly and ping support with canned response.

Jordan (SRE): opened Datadog support ticket 98765, included logs and request IDs, asked for ETA. Ticket note: 'upstream resets and ingestion backlog growth since 02:02 UTC'.

Maya (eng-ops): handing off to night oncall — I'm staying available for 20m. Handoff notes: throttled metric-forwarder, CW fallback enabled, ticket 98765 open, runbook updated, customer comm drafted.

Alex (oncall): :thumbsup: Thanks — pass to @Maya if anything degrades. If Datadog reports capacity restored, we'll gradually re-enable push rate.

Maya (eng-ops): ack — will monitor dashboards and local host logs. Increasing local logging retention to capture missing events for replay:```bash
kubectl -n telemetry patch ds telemetry-logger --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/0/value","value":"3600"}]'```
-> retention bumped to +1h

Jordan (SRE): final note before handoff: set alerts to suppress noisy symptoms (dd_ingest_alert -> suppressed) and create an observability-ticket for follow-up (investigate better fallback & circuit-breaker on push).

incident-bot: Incident note appended: participants updated, handoff recorded.

Ella (product): posting status now and notifying support playbook. Will update once Datadog provides ETA. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Maya (eng-ops): taking over watch. I'll escalate to account team if SLA risk. leaving this thread open for updates.
